hypotheses.justification: The statement uses only these hypotheses. `Homothetic`, `latticeMap` and `scalarGL` need [CommRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K]. `unitOfNeZero` (Def_LatticeTreeOrbital.lean:505) also needs [IsFractionRing R K]: it is `Units.mk0 (algebraMap R K r)`, and its nonzeroness proof uses `IsFractionRing.injective`, which in Mathlib's Localization/FractionRing.lean only assumes CommRing R, CommRing K and [IsFractionRing R K]. IsDomain R is mentioned nowhere in the statement. The proof goes through `pointwise_smul_eq_latticeMap`, which carries [IsDomain R] as a section variable but does not use it: its proof only uses `Submodule.mem_smul_pointwise_iff_exists`, `mem_latticeMap_scalarGL` (needs CommRing R, Field K, Algebra R K), `unitOfNeZero_coe` and `algebraMap_smul`. So both lemmas can take `omit [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] in`. Alternatively, if `pointwise_smul_eq_latticeMap` is left unchanged, IsDomain R can be rebuilt locally from the other hypotheses via `(IsFractionRing.isDomain_iff_isField R K).mpr (Field.toIsField K)` (Mathlib FractionRing.lean:245). No degenerate case breaks this: R cannot be trivial, because algebraMap R K is injective into a field.
